newsitem.title: PERU: Venezuela sees positive interest rates by mid-year.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sees positive interest rates by mid-year.

text.p: Venezuela will achieve its goal getting inflation below interest rates by mid-year, provided that inflation continues its present downward trend, Venezuelan Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said Wednesday.

"The aim continues to be to reach a situation of positive real interest rates by mid-year," Casas told Reuters in an interview during a break from a meeting of central bank officials from the Americas and Spain.
Deposit rates in commercial banks currently average little over 10 percent, despite an inflation rate over the last 12 months of more than 75 percent.
Venezuela had hoped to reach positive real interest rates soon after implementing an economic reform program in April 1996 but had been hampered by high inflation, Casas said.
"It was thought that inflation was going to be a bit lower than it is. We have had what is called inertial inflation which is very difficult to break," he said.

Inflation in 1996 was 103.2 percent. But monthly price rises dropped to 1.6 percent in March -- the lowest monthly rate for five years -- and accumulated inflation over the first three months was one quarter of that in the same period in 1996.
"If we achieve (inflation) in the second quarter that is about the same proportion, I think that by July we could be thinking of positive real interste rates," Casas said.
